handoff.purpose: Review check(): snapshot integrity validation, phantom-list detection, unreached-class comparisons, and good-news direction.

symbols.name: check
symbols.note: Main comparison function. Loads snapshot, validates schema/digest/counts, detects phantom entries, and emits DriftItem findings for islands, unknown, shims, engine disagreements, newly reached, and vanished modules. May write a missing snapshot if write_missing is set.

claims.text: A missing snapshot FAILS unless write_missing is set, which is the explicit 'record a baseline' action rather than the default.
claims.why: When snapshot is None and write_missing is False, DriftReport(ok=False, first_run=True, ...) is returned; when write_missing is True, write_snapshot is called and ok=True.

claims.text: The previous default -- write it and report OK -- meant rm docs/architecture-state .json was a green run, and a green run against nothing is exactly what this file exists to make impossible.
claims.why: The code returns ok=False for missing snapshot unless write_missing is explicitly set, so a missing snapshot is not a green run by default.

claims.text: The exact failure this whole module exists to prevent: a number in an artifact that no longer matches the list beside it.
claims.why: For each stored count, if it differs from the real length of the corresponding list, an INVALID_SNAPSHOT DriftItem is appended.

claims.text: A count matching its own list proves only internal arithmetic. These check the lists against reality and against each other, so an entry cannot be pre-seeded to suppress a finding that has not landed yet.
claims.why: The code checks phantom_islands (old_islands - old_modules), phantom entries for unknown/shims (set(list) - old_modules), phantom_test_only (old_test_only - (old_islands|old_unknown|old_shims)), and phantom_dark (old_dark - read_names). All are checks against other lists or against the environment reads.

claims.text: An accepted island is deliberately absent from the baseline (:func:`write_snapshot`), so the baseline alone would read it as 'reached' and call it BECAME ISLAND the moment the module also appears in modules.
claims.why: The claim about write_snapshot's behavior is not verifiable from this chunk; write_snapshot is defined elsewhere in the file.

claims.text: The acceptance is itself a record that it is an island, so it counts toward what the snapshot knows -- without suppressing anything.
claims.why: The code uses accepted_keys to build known_unreached, but how acceptances are used in comparisons is not fully visible in this chunk (the acceptance handling appears later).

claims.text: Intersecting with modules is the teeth behind the subset rule above: an island entry the snapshot's own module list does not back is a hand-edit, and a hand-edit must not be able to suppress the finding it was written to hide.
claims.why: baselined_islands = old_islands & old_modules; phantom_islands check flags islands not in modules; in the island loop, modules in baselined_islands are skipped (unless test coverage changed), so a hand-edited island that is not in modules would not be treated as baselined.

claims.text: BECAME ISLAND means 'it was REACHED and is not any more'. A module the snapshot recorded as unknown or as an unreached shim was never reached, so it must not be described that way when it degrades into an island.
claims.why: known_unreached includes old_islands|old_unknown|old_shims intersected with old_modules, plus accepted keys of kind island/unknown/shim. In the island loop, was_reached = mod in old_modules and mod not in known_unreached; if was_reached is False, kind is NEW_ISLAND instead of BECAME_ISLAND.

claims.text: Same shape as islands, deliberately not merged into them: the finding a reader gets has to say WHICH kind of unreached this is, because the three remedies are three different sentences.
claims.why: The loop handles 'unknown' and 'shims' separately, using distinct prefixes (unknown:, shim:) and distinct kinds (NEW_UNKNOWN, NEW_SHIM), and distinct remedy calls.

claims.text: What they share is the property that used to be missing entirely -- a module nothing reaches is COUNTED, is named, and blocks until somebody explains it.
claims.why: Both unknown and shims are emitted as DriftItems with kind NEW_UNKNOWN or NEW_SHIM, which are blocking findings (the function returns ok=False when items are non-empty, as implied by the overall design).

claims.text: It is reported, never merged: merging it is how a dead-branch import used to make its target 'reachable'
claims.why: The loop only appends DriftItem with kind ENGINE_DISAGREEMENT; it does not add the edge to any other list.

claims.text: new_unreached, not new_islands: a module that moved from island to shim (or to unknown) is still reached by nothing, and announcing 'something reaches it now' would be the same false-green in a new costume.
claims.why: The good-news loop checks 'if mod not in new_unreached' where new_unreached = new_islands | new_unknown | new_shims, so a module that moved among unreached classes will not be reported as NOW_REACHED.

claims.text: The structural index has this import edge and the reachability walk does not.
claims.why: The claim about what the structural index and reachability walk contain is not verifiable from this chunk; it depends on the construction of new_index_extra and old_index_extra.

claims.text: The snapshot is unreadable, hand-edited or self-inconsistent; re-baseline (--refresh) after checking what changed
claims.why: The remedy text is a string; whether re-baselining is actually permitted or blocked by other rules is not determinable from this chunk.

observations.what: The digest mismatch check appends an INVALID_SNAPSHOT item but does not return early, unlike the __error__ and schema checks which return immediately.
phantom_dark compares old_dark against result.switches.env_switches; this depends on the completeness of env_switches, which is not visible in this chunk.
accepted_keys is parsed from acceptances; the split on ':' assumes the format 'kind:module'. If the format changes, the known_unreached set could be wrong.

The good-news loop uses old_set & new_modules for each prefix, but for 'island:' it uses old_islands, which includes islands that may not be in old_modules; however, the phantom check ensures old_islands is a subset of old_modules, so the intersection is consistent.
